1) Answer

Yes. There is clear, public, and repeated evidence in Lisa Nandy’s parliamentary record and frontbench roles that she prioritises human rights:

- Hong Kong and civil liberties: As Shadow Foreign Secretary, on 1 July 2020 she condemned Hong Kong’s national security law as “deeply shocking,” pressed for practical protections for Hongkongers (including details of the BNO route), and urged UK leadership on accountability and policing abuses; she also pursued a UN special rapporteur for Hong Kong in a written parliamentary question on 2 July 2020. ([hansard.parliament.uk](https://hansard.parliament.uk/Commons/2020-07-01/debates/7A4917D6-E522-4589-8649-B9537A1051EA/HongKongNationalSecurityLegislation?utm_source=openai))

- Uyghurs and sanctions: She consistently pressed for robust action over mass abuses in Xinjiang. In the Commons on 22 March 2021 she urged stronger, earlier UK sanctions on Chinese officials and challenged government delay; in a 16 December 2020 debate she highlighted forced labour and “mass atrocities” tied to UK supply chains. These are concrete, recordable interventions in defence of human rights. ([hansard.parliament.uk](https://hansard.parliament.uk/Commons/2021-03-22/debates/7E304076-1DAF-482C-B4AD-FFFDB8813E53/HumanRightsUpdate?utm_source=openai))

- Anti‑corruption and human‑rights enforcement: On 26 April 2021 she welcomed the UK’s new Global Anti‑Corruption Sanctions regime and explicitly tied corruption controls to enforcing human-rights accountability, urging adequate enforcement resources. ([hansard.parliament.uk](https://hansard.parliament.uk/commons/2021-04-26/debates/0AE0D378-E2D2-4CBB-9CEB-425A70549ED2/GlobalAnti-CorruptionSanctions?utm_source=openai))

- Yemen and humanitarian law: On 8 February 2021 she argued that the UK cannot be “both peacemaker and arms dealer,” calling out UK arms sales feeding the Yemen war and urging policy consistent with human‑rights leadership. ([hansard.parliament.uk](https://hansard.parliament.uk/commons/2021-02-08/debates/DD75DAB2-90FB-42FF-B3EC-095A91F0C49B/Yemen?utm_source=openai))

- International law and humanitarian protection in Gaza: As Labour’s shadow international development lead, on 17 April 2024 she urged restoring UK funding to UNRWA to avert famine, and said the UK should back accountability through the ICC and ICJ—clear commitments to international humanitarian and human‑rights law. ([theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/apr/17/lisa-nandy-urges-support-un-relief-agency-for-palestinians?utm_source=openai))

Taken together—on China/Hong Kong, Uyghur abuses, sanctions policy, Yemen arms exports and humanitarian protection—Nandy’s actions and statements over multiple years consistently prioritise human rights and the rule of law.

  [2] Reasoning 1: Official, verbatim transcript of parliamentary proceedings; primary source for MPs’ words and actions.
  [3] Reasoning 2: Directly records Nandy’s statements on Hong Kong (01/07/2020), Uyghurs (16/12/2020; 22/03/2021 debate), Yemen (08/02/2021), and sanctions (26/04/2021), which are the core evidence here. ([hansard.parliament.uk](https://hansard.parliament.uk/Commons/2020-07-01/debates/7A4917D6-E522-4589-8649-B9537A1051EA/HongKongNationalSecurityLegislation?utm_source=openai))

  [2] Reasoning 1: Official UK government publication; authoritative for UK positions at the UN.
  [3] Reasoning 2: Contextualises the multilateral human‑rights framework Nandy engaged with and referenced in her interventions. ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/speeches/joint-statement-on-the-human-rights-situation-in-xinjiang-and-recent-developments-in-hong-kong?utm_source=openai))

- [1] Source: The Guardian
  [2] Reasoning 1: Major UK newspaper with rigorous editorial standards and on‑the‑record sourcing.
  [3] Reasoning 2: Provides contemporaneous reporting of Nandy’s 17 April 2024 Washington trip and her calls to resume UNRWA funding and back ICC/ICJ accountability, complementing the parliamentary record.
